text:
mira: Heads-up — p95 and p99 latency on the inference gateway just jumped after the canary deploy (canary-2027-04-03). Seeing lots of `504` and backend timeouts.
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Incident created: INC-2027-1003 — Elevated gateway timeouts and 5xx after canary deploy. Severity: P1. Paging on-call.
mira: Metrics: p95 from ~120ms -> 1.2s, p99 from ~260ms -> 5.6s. Error rate 5xx from 0.2% -> 6.8%. Canary traffic was ~15% of prod.
jamie: I'm oncall. I'm digging into the canary pod logs. Which commit rolled?
mira: Canary hash: ab3c9f2 (image: rf-infer:canary-ab3c9f2). Rollout started 1824999800.
alex: Repro on staging? I ran a quick load against the canary endpoint and hit a long tail too. Attaching tail of gateway logs.
alex: ```
[proxy] 2027-04-03T10:12:34Z GET /v1/generate 504 upstream timed out after 30000ms
[runtime] 2027-04-03T10:12:34Z model request id=xyz took 31000ms kv-cache miss
```
jamie: Looks like requests are hanging in the runtime layer — KV cache misses and a ~31s wall time. Canary config bumped `max_seq_length` default to 4096 in the new model config; that could change token processing and kernel selection.
mira: Could be an input distribution issue causing long sequences? We've been observing more long-context prompts from a customer test suite.
ana: (Note: I am not in participants list; replace with ana).
ana: Sorry mis-typed — ana here. We saw some customers hitting interactive sessions with long prefixes. Could that cause catastrophic batching?
jamie: Hypothesis: new kernel selection path for sequence >2048 falls back to slower code path, causing timeouts when combined with batch size.
luke: Quick mitigation options: 1) rollback canary to previous image, 2) reduce canary traffic to 0%, 3) tune gateway timeouts and shed long-context requests.
maya: We should assess customer impact before rollback. Any active 504 spikes causing user-facing outages?
mira: Alerting shows a handful of enterprise customers (IDs: C-110, C-233) with increased errors on generate endpoints. Support already flagged two tickets.
jamie: Rollback plan: if we can't identify a safe mitigation in 10 minutes, I'll roll the canary back to image rf-infer:stable-20270401. We need approval.
ana: (again) — ana: I approve rollback. Product agrees; customers affected are in SLAs.
alex: I'll prepare the rollback manifest. Command to run: 
```bash
kubectl set image deploy/inference-gateway inference=rf-infer:stable-20270401 -n prod-canary
```
jamie: Before we do that, can we try lowering `inference_gateway.max_batch_size` on canary to 1 to see if latency improves? That would reduce batching and might avoid the slow path.
luke: Lowering batch size is lower-risk and faster than rollback. But it will increase CPU per-request and could raise costs. Still worth trying.
mira: Go for the batch-size change first. Alex, can you push the quick override?
alex: Pushing patch to canary svc now. Patch: `max_batch_size: 1`. Applying...
deploy-bot: Deploy started: deploy/ingress-override-1825001305 by alex.
alex: Patch applied. Waiting 30s to observe.
jamie: Metrics already warming — p95 dropped to ~220ms, p99 down to ~380ms on canary. Error rate back to 0.5% in last 45s.
mira: Nice. Any sign of backlog in runtime or OOM?
alex: No OOMs. CPU increased but within headroom. No new 5xx except a couple of stale duplicates.
jamie: Given this improvement, we can hold on rollback. But we need a long-term fix before promoting this canary to prod. Opening follow-up: root cause investigation for kernel selection path and default sequence length.
incident-bot: Incident INC-2027-1003 status: mitigated -> monitoring. Triage owner: jamie. Follow-up ticket: TICKET-7421 (investigate slow path for >2048 sequences).
ana: ana: Support will update affected customers and patch notes.
mira: I'll schedule a postmortem and include workload traces. Thanks everyone for quick coordination. :thumbsup:
jamie: oncall Handoff: I'll keep monitoring for 2h then hand to next oncall (alex).
alex: ack. I'll watch the dashboards and keep rollback ready.
maya: Logging note: capture a full runtime trace for a 31s request (request id=xyz) and attach to TICKET-7421.
jamie: Closing thread for now; re-open if errors creep back up.
incident-bot: Incident INC-2027-1003 closed (mitigated).
